Two years ago, Sonos expanded from the wireless speaker sector into the over-ear headphone market. Now, Sonos appears to be preparing to launch a higher-end successor model with added artificial intelligence features.

Sonos Ace Ultra over-ear headphones are set to debut

Chris Welch reported for Bloomberg that Sonos is developing the Ace Ultra, a high-end successor to its 2024 Ace headphones.

Application documents filed with the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) and discovered on Monday revealed the product name and showed up to five colour options, a richer range compared to the original model's black and white only.

Sonos is planning to hold a product launch event in September, and the timing of this filing suggests the Ace Ultra is very likely to make its first appearance at that event.

The documents also contain technical clues indicating that the new headphones may support voice command functionality.

According to Bloomberg, CEO Tom Conrad acknowledged that the original headphones lacked sufficient integration with the whole-home audio system when launched, failing to stand out in a competitive market.

This time, Sonos appears to be tying its hardware more directly to a broader artificial intelligence strategy.

Conrad described the company's opportunity as conversational computing and predictive intelligence in the home, running through Sonos hardware in different rooms and learning the usage habits of household members.

The company has extended Sonos voice control to operate smart home systems such as Philips Hue and Lutron Caseta.

Meanwhile, Apple's upgraded AirPods Max 2 launched in March this year, equipped with an H2 chip, enhanced noise cancellation, and live translation support. Siri artificial intelligence features are also expected to extend to AirPods via iOS 27.
